bull.b: Record revenue, substantial bookings, and a large backlog provide meaningful forward demand visibility across Launch and Space Systems. With about 45.5% of backlog expected to convert within 12 months, the company has a substantial contracted base supporting continued growth over the next several quarters.

Gross-margin improvement from roughly 9% in 2022 to about 37% TTM indicates better unit economics as Rocket Lab scales. Q2 performance above guidance further supports operating progress, although sustained benefits will depend on product mix, acquisition integration, and continued execution.

The materially lower leverage ratio gives Rocket Lab greater financial flexibility than it had in 2024. A stronger capital structure can support Neutron development, production expansion, and strategic investments while reducing balance-sheet pressure as the company works toward sustainable profitability.

bear.b: Rocket Lab is still consuming substantial cash to fund operations and investment, despite improving free-cash-flow trends. Continued negative operating and free cash flow can increase funding needs and constrain capital allocation, particularly while Neutron development and production scaling require elevated spending.

The shift of Neutron’s first flight into 2027 delays Rocket Lab’s expansion into medium-lift launch services and postpones potential access to a broader market. The revised timeline also shows that manufacturing and testing milestones remain important execution hurdles before commercial operations can begin.

Lower guided gross margins after Q2’s strong performance indicate that profitability remains sensitive to Space Systems mix and acquisition contributions. Initial Mynaric pressure may persist while synergies are realized, making the path toward sustainable operating profitability less predictable over the next several quarters.
